question: What was the mood in the mail on September 11?

steps.text: I'm treating the question as being about the mood in the mail on September 11, most likely 2001, and laying out a plan first. answer:
The mood in the mail on September 11, 2001 was shock and worry. Practical, subdued business mail ran alongside it. I'm reading "September 11" as 2001.

- **Shock and concern for others.** Outside correspondents wrote things like "We are shocked and distressed beyond words at the cowardly terrorist attack on innocent Americans." A family note said "we are fine, except devastated about what is happening to the Country," and ended "Stay safe all of you." A contact at HSBC wrote, "my window looks right at WTC i saw the whole thing. are your employees over there?" People were checking whether friends and colleagues were safe: "What's the word on these plane crashes into the WTCs?"
- **Staff in New York.** One person described seeing "the second trade tower collapse. It is truly horrible," and said she was still waiting to hear where her husband was. Another wrote, "Unfathomable tragedy," and added "We're going to hold our 11:30 call in an attempt to maintain a sense of normalcy."
- **Official tone from Enron.** The chairman's office said the Enron Building in Houston would close for the rest of the day, the New York and Washington offices were also closed, and "all employees have been accounted for." It also said "Let's keep all the victims of these tragedies in our thoughts and prayers."
- **Anxious analysis.** An internal analyst's report opened with "US is under attack. We are in state of emergency. Casualties are likely to be in the thousands." It also warned of a "flight to quality" in the markets. A later update covered closed exchanges, a flight ban and US forces on "highest alert."
- **Work disrupted, then picked up.** One person wrote that "In light of this mornings events, most of the trading floor is leaving," so a meeting was pushed back. The California ISO warned of possible difficulty running that day's and the next day's markets. A gas operations note said "We didn't have a complete trading session," but pipelines would roll nominations forward. By day's end, a draft press release announced "the resumption of trading tomorrow." Some ordinary mail went on regardless, such as a contract-settlement issues list.

The counts come from mail_counts. The store holds 137 emails dated September 11, and only 13 of them contain one of my attack-related phrases, so those exact-phrase matches are a lower bound. Mail with those phrases rose from 5 in the week ending September 9 to 94 in the week ending September 16. The search results come from a sample of the day's mail, not all of it. The sources are internal Enron mail, mail from outside correspondents, and exchange and market-operator notices. None of it is forwarded press.

Just a note to check on all our beloveds on this horrible day. We are glued  
to the tv while we carry on our daily activities in Columbia.  Actually I

We have had several calls this morning to inquire if we are o.k. Yes we are  
fine, except devastated about what is happening to the Country. 
On a routine note, we have painters painting our garage, workers putting on  
new siding at our rental house across the street, A furnace man putting in a  
new energy efficient furnace also in the rental house. Most of these workers  
are in good spirits..some mostly unaware of what is going on.  The furnace  
man thought the answer to our problems was that everybody should carry more  
guns. Life goes on at many different levels. 
Stay safe all of you.  Stay off the planes and out of government buildings.  
Love Bonnie
